summary: Atherton packs just 7,030 residents into five square miles of flat-to-gently-rolling San Mateo County terrain — no downtown, no commercial district, essentially no sidewalks — yet its median home value exceeds $2 million on a median household income above $250,000, producing a price-to-income ratio around 8:1 that makes even its extraordinarily high earners stretch to buy. The town sits on the oak-studded floor of the San Francisco Peninsula between the Santa Cruz Mountains to the west and the bay marshlands to the east, close enough to Sand Hill Road's venture-capital corridor and Stanford University to function as a bedroom community for the highest tier of the tech and finance economy, while offering almost nothing in the way of retail, restaurants, or nightlife within its own borders — daily errands mean driving to neighboring Menlo Park or Redwood City. The climate is genuinely mild, averaging 68°F daytime highs with over nine hours of daily sunshine and cool 51°F nights that rarely demand air conditioning or heavy coats. With 85.9 percent of adults holding at least a bachelor's degree and 55.5 percent a graduate degree, the economic texture is overwhelmingly professional-class, and the 3.3 percent poverty rate reflects that concentration. Atherton is less a town than a residential preserve — the tradeoff for its space, quiet, and proximity to Peninsula job centers is that nearly every dimension of daily life exists somewhere else.
